name: Texas
standard: Texas Gov't Code Ch. 2054 Subch. M; 1 TAC Ch. 206 (websites) and Ch. 213 (EIR). In-force rule text references Section 508 (WCAG 2.0 AA via 36 CFR 1194 App. C §702.10); WCAG 2.1 AA applies through the DOJ Title II rule, and DIR's 2026 amendments cite it directly.

laws.summary: Requires state agencies and institutions of higher education to provide accessible electronic and information resources and directs DIR to adopt accessibility rules.
Sets accessibility requirements for state agency websites by reference to Section 508 standards and Chapter 213.
Requires a published accessibility policy, an EIR Accessibility Coordinator, a compliance plan and goals, and DIR notice of coordinator vacancies within 30 days.

laws.cite: 28 CFR Part 35, Subpart H (ADA Title II web/mobile rule, 2024; compliance dates extended by DOJ IFR effective 2026-04-20)
laws.summary: Requires state and local government web content and mobile apps to conform to WCAG 2.1 AA, with compliance dates now 2027-04-26 (population 50,000+) and 2028-04-26 (smaller entities and special districts).

policy_docs.title: Texas Register 2026-03-13 — proposed amendments to 1 TAC Ch. 213

applies_to: State agencies and public institutions of higher education, covering websites, software, documents, multimedia, hardware and hosted services. Local governments are not covered by Ch. 206/213; the ADA Title II floor applies to them.

deadlines.what: ADA Title II floor: state government and local entities with population 50,000+ must conform to WCAG 2.1 AA (extended from 2026-04-24 by the 2026 DOJ IFR).
ADA Title II floor: local entities under 50,000 population and special district governments (extended from 2027-04-26).
DIR proposed Ch. 213 amendments: coordinator renamed Digital Accessibility Officer, DOJ Title II rule incorporated, ACR defined against WCAG. Final adoption not confirmed.

requires: Designated EIR Accessibility Coordinator (proposed: Digital Accessibility Officer); notify DIR within 30 days of vacancy
Agency-approved plan and measurable goals to bring EIR into compliance
Exceptions approved in writing by the agency head (Gov't Code § 2054.460); statewide exemptions only via DIR
Third-party or qualified-staff accessibility testing for EIR projects over $500,000
DIR accessibility survey and biennial compliance review
mobile: explicit — the proposed Ch. 213 applies the DOJ Title II rule to 'web content and mobile applications'; the current rule covers EIR generally.
procurement: EIR procured or changed through contracts must comply with Ch. 206/213 unless excepted; ACR based on a VPAT is the documentation vehicle.
enforcement: Agency-level accessibility policy and contact; DIR oversight via survey and compliance reviews; ADA Title II complaints to US DOJ.
notes: Conflict: university pages say Ch. 213 revisions took effect in June 2026, but the adoption notice was not found. The last confirmed § 213.21 amendment is 2019-12-12 and § 206.50 is 2018-02-15. Before relying on the WCAG 2.1 wording or the 'Digital Accessibility Officer' title, confirm the adopted text in the Texas Register.
